title: Token-level Data Selection for Safe LLM Fine-tuning
topic: Social Aspects->Fairness, Equity, Justice and Safety
claim: Sample-level selection discards whole examples and loses useful content; token-level selection removes only unsafe tokens, improving both safety and utility.
layout: 2 panels: left flow diagram with two branches, right scatter plot
description: The left panel is a flow diagram. A legend at the top defines unsafe tokens (solid red), discarded tokens (red with an X) and safe tokens (light blue). Benign samples (green box) and harmful samples (pink box) appear as rows of token squares. An arrow splits into two branches. The upper branch, sample-level selection (blue), keeps only whole benign samples, so the selected data is small. It leads to a customized LLM drawn as a neural network. The lower branch, token-level selection (orange), keeps both sample types but crosses out the unsafe tokens, and leads to a customized LLM with a green shield. The right panel is a scatter plot of Safety (%) against Utility (%). It shows blue sample-level markers and orange token-level markers for r=0.3, 0.5 and 0.7, plus a black X for the StandardSFT baseline. The orange markers sit in the upper right.
caption: Left: High-level comparison of sample-level and token-level selection methods for safe LLM customization. Right: Comparison of sample-level and token-level selection methods on different custom datasets with varying ratios of harmful data r. Our token-level data selection method achieves significant improvements in both safety and utility compared to the sample-level one.
abstract: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) on custom datasets has become a standard approach for adapting these models to specific domains and applications. However, recent studies have shown that such fine-tuning can lead to significant degradation in the model's safety. Existing defense methods operate at the sample level and often suffer from an unsatisfactory trade-off between safety and utility. To address this limitation, we perform a systematic token-level diagnosis of safety degradation during fine-tuning. Based on this, we propose token-level data selection for safe LLM fine-tuning (TOSS), a novel framework that quantifies the safety risk of each token by measuring the loss difference between a safety-degraded model and a utility-oriented model. This token-level granularity enables accurate identification and removal of unsafe tokens, thereby preserving valuable task-specific information. In addition, we introduce a progressive refinement strategy, TOSS-Pro, which iteratively enhances the safety-degraded model's ability to identify unsafe tokens. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach robustly safeguards LLMs during fine-tuning while achieving superior downstream task performance, significantly outperforming existing sample-level defense methods. Our code is available at https://github.com/Polly-LYP/TOSS.
